ratingVocabulary.preserved: The model represents the distinction directly enough for the tested consumer class.
ratingVocabulary.partial: The distinction can be reconstructed or mapped, but is not a stable first-class separation.
ratingVocabulary.collapsed: The model merges materially different concepts or forces them into peer categories.
ratingVocabulary.omitted: The model intentionally does not represent the distinction and therefore cannot be the complete practical contract.
ratingVocabulary.candidate: The model represents the distinction, but CA1-CA4 physical/provider experiments are still required to validate it.

A_tactic_lifecycle_tree.reason: ATT&CK tactics and techniques explicitly separate why/how, but one technique can serve multiple tactics and the structure is an observed-behavior coordinate rather than a bound capability contract.

B_tool_artifact_tree.reason: Tools, carriers, resources, and mechanisms are peers, so semantic effect must be inferred from implementation identity.

C_pure_relation_graph.reason: Semantic effects are explicit but mechanism is intentionally absent.

D_orthogonal_capability_contract.reason: Semantic transition and mechanism are distinct coordinates.

A_tactic_lifecycle_tree.reason: Technique/sub-technique detail can mention carrier but does not make carrier orthogonal to mechanism.

B_tool_artifact_tree.reason: PowerShell, macro, installer, exploit, credential, worm, and C2-like categories mix carrier, mechanism, resource, and architecture.

C_pure_relation_graph.reason: Neither mechanism nor carrier is represented.

D_orthogonal_capability_contract.reason: Mechanism and carrier remain separate and exact provider realization is another coordinate.

A_tactic_lifecycle_tree.reason: Reconnaissance/vulnerability-scanning and exploitation behaviors can be mapped, but target-specific opportunity, attempt, receipt, and consequence are not the primary ontology boundary.

B_tool_artifact_tree.reason: Scanner/exploit/tool identity tends to stand in for opportunity and action status.

C_pure_relation_graph.reason: Opportunity and consequence can be world relations, but provider attempt/receipt semantics are absent.

D_orthogonal_capability_contract.reason: Opportunity/preconditions, action binding, provider receipt, observations, and independent consequence are separate.

A_tactic_lifecycle_tree.reason: Tactic order suggests progression but does not itself encode causal precondition dependency; Attack Flow is a separate project for this reason.

B_tool_artifact_tree.reason: A tool inventory does not encode why one action enables another.

C_pure_relation_graph.reason: A transition can create world preconditions consumed by a later transition.

D_orthogonal_capability_contract.reason: Relation transitions plus explicit preconditions compose naturally while keeping operational realization.

A_tactic_lifecycle_tree.reason: Offensive ATT&CK and defensive D3FEND are separate knowledge structures even when they alter opposite directions of the same world relation.

B_tool_artifact_tree.reason: Red and Blue product/tool families become different top-level categories.

C_pure_relation_graph.reason: Acquire/revoke authority, expand/isolate reachability, persist/eradicate continuity, and exploit/harden opportunity are naturally opposite relation changes.

D_orthogonal_capability_contract.reason: The same relation grammar is retained while objective, authority, provider, and direction differ; CA3/CA4 must physically falsify this.

A_tactic_lifecycle_tree.reason: Techniques can map across implementations, but exact provider/fidelity applicability is external metadata.

B_tool_artifact_tree.reason: Replacing provider/carrier changes the apparent capability identity even when semantics remain stable.

C_pure_relation_graph.reason: World semantics are provider-independent, but this is also why fidelity and mechanism distinctions disappear.

D_orthogonal_capability_contract.reason: Semantic identity can survive provider replacement while provider and fidelity remain exact evidence coordinates.

A_tactic_lifecycle_tree.reason: Propagation can be expressed as sequences of techniques but autonomy/delegation is not a stable orthogonal property.

B_tool_artifact_tree.reason: Virus/worm labels capture some propagation architecture but bind it to malware categories and carriers.

C_pure_relation_graph.reason: Repeated relation changes can be represented but controller-directed versus delegated/autonomous continuation is easy to erase.

D_orthogonal_capability_contract.reason: Control mode is explicit; CA3 must test whether self-propagation adds value beyond repeated controller-issued movement.

A_tactic_lifecycle_tree.reason: ATT&CK describes adversary behavior and detection knowledge but is not a truth-authority protocol.

B_tool_artifact_tree.reason: Sensor, detector, SIEM/EDR, analysis tool, and responder are easily grouped together as defensive tools.

C_pure_relation_graph.reason: Knowledge/observability relations exist but derivation provenance and provider receipts are not sufficient by themselves.

D_orthogonal_capability_contract.reason: Native evidence, fallible observations/detections, provider receipt, and independent consequence remain distinct coordinates/planes.

A_tactic_lifecycle_tree.reason: Technique metadata and operational knowledge may imply these properties but they are not the semantic identity boundary.

B_tool_artifact_tree.reason: Tool identity may predict these properties but makes portability and comparison difficult.

C_pure_relation_graph.reason: Equivalent final state transitions can have radically different exposure, latency, rollback, and cleanup.

D_orthogonal_capability_contract.reason: The properties are explicit optional coordinates; later experiments must show which ones deserve Agent-visible projection versus evidence-only retention.

decision.reason: It is the only candidate that preserves the semantic transition spine while retaining operational distinctions required by materially different carriers/providers and by Security's existing authority/evidence laws.
decision.scope: CA0 research coordinate only; not a production schema or public enum.
decision.nextPressure: CA1-CA4 must try to break the retained model with physical/provider consumers before CA5 may promote any shared binding.
